title: The Impact of Visitor Activities on Cave Damage: A Study of Vandalism at the Liang Kabori Site, Indonesia
content: This research aims to analyze the impact of visitor activities on damage in Liang Kabori Cave with a focus on acts of vandalism, such as graffiti, taking cave stalactites and stalagmites, and environmental pollution in the cave area. This research uses a descriptive qualitative method with an archaeological approach, including data collection, processing, and interpretation. Data were obtained from literature study and field survey through observation, interview, and documentation. Observations were made of archaeological objects, the cave environment, and visitor behavior towards the Site. Interviews involved the caretaker who acts as the party responsible for maintaining, supervising, and providing information about the site and visitors in order to explore their understanding of the importance of cave preservation and awareness of the prohibition of vandalism in the cave. The documentation was conducted to obtain data related to the forms of vandalism damage to the site. The results showed that the high number of visitors can provide potential damage to the site. Uncontrolled visitor activities often cause damage, especially in the form of vandalism. Therefore, a more systematic and collaborative approach is needed, by increasing the number and capacity of caretakers, developing strict visit regulations, strengthening the site management system, and expanding the role of local communities as conservation partners, so that this site is maintained as an important part of the nation's cultural heritage. This research is expected to serve as a basis for conservation efforts in Liang Kabori Cave as well as a reference for the management of other caves in Indonesia.
